name: inprocess-obi-apb-cv32e40p-pulp-timer-zipdma-f1f6
description: The same one-CPU/one-APB3-target/one-ZipDMA declaration the Ibex replacement runs, with the CPU profile swapped from configs/cpus/ibex_rvfi_local to the pinned configs/cpus/cv32e40p_rvfi_local. Nothing else about the build changes: the entry reads the CPU's OBI endpoints, its declared boot contract (PC_BOOT = {boot_addr_i[31:2],2'b0} at 0x10000) and its assigned RVFI observation fields from the profile.
notes: The scenario is the Ibex timer/DMA declaration with its cpu_profile line changed; the target, DMA, windows, image and every record are the same bytes. That is the whole profile swap the P0-1 CPU replacement claims.

cv32e40p_rvfi_local declares the same OBI instruction/data masters as ibex_rvfi_local, so the entry's CPU bus selection, the obi_processor_memory_adapter and the target routing are unchanged. Its boot formula is the pinned external_designs/cv32e40p/rtl/cv32e40p_if_stage.sv PC_BOOT = {boot_addr_i[31:2], 2'b0} with boot_addr_i = 0x10000 held by the profile's port_actions, so the bootstrap image lands at the RAM base 0x10000 instead of Ibex's 0x10080; build_firmware already places the bootstrap at layout['boot'] and jumps to the fixed main loop, so no image or address is special-cased for this CPU.

The local top assigns only rvfi_valid/rvfi_order/rvfi_insn/rvfi_pc_rdata. F1 compares the observed retirement count, order and installed words from those fields; it never claims rvfi_intr, rvfi_trap or a writeback channel the profile does not export.

F5 delivers the timer's real irq_o to the CPU's declared machine-external line irq_i[11] (cv32e40p_irq_receipt_contract SOURCE_ID=11); the acceptance evidence is the real controller decision plus irq_ack_o/irq_id_o and the IF-stage exception PC, not an RVFI intr because that field is not driven.

The timer profile, the ZipDMA profile, the DMA capability and the F5 trigger/status facts are reused byte for byte from configs/scenarios/inprocess-obi-apb-ibex-timer-zipdma-f1f6.json, so the only difference between the two runs is the CPU profile line.
